A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 22-page versions of the same Attention-Shifting paper, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered pages match except for the first-page version stamp and Equation (5).

before.justification: v1 reports original ToFU and TDEC experiments, ablations and robustness analyses, plus biomedical unlearning results in Table 15 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains the original ToFU, TDEC and biomedical unlearning results, including the experimental analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: Equation (5) changes the retention term from KL(model attention || reinforced target attention) to KL(reinforced target attention || model attention). KL is asymmetric, so this locally revises the stated training objective. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is identical: ToFU, TDEC, Wikitext, LAMBADA and PubMedQA, including biomedical unlearning, adversarial queries, overlapping knowledge and sequential unlearning scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain GA, NPO, IHL and ULD, including the same CE/KL retention variants. Comparator membership is unchanged in both main-text and appendix experiments.

E3.justification: The stated splits, sample sizes, model configurations, metrics, training settings and evaluation procedures are identical. No separate experimental-protocol revision accompanies the loss change.

E4.justification: The retained-data, ASP/AKL, adversarial-prompt, overlapping-knowledge, adapter-placement and hyperparameter analyses are unchanged, including Figures 3, 5 and 9 and Tables 4–7.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including Figure 7's standard-deviation bands. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative result entries are identical across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains AS's TR of 0.97, FQ of 0.17, neighbouring accuracy of 0.76 and general accuracy of 0.80.

T1.justification: Reversing the asymmetric KL arguments substantively revises the mathematical definition of the retention objective in Equation (5). Appendix A's attention analysis and suppression-loss gradient derivation remain unchanged; no analysis of the revised retention term is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about selective unlearning, hallucination resistance and knowledge retention, including the claimed ToFU and TDEC advantages.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations and limitations are identical, including the distinction between behavioural suppression and representational erasure, sensitivity to noisy data and limitations for generative tasks.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, adapter placement, hyperparameters, hardware, data-processing descriptions and GPT-4 evaluation prompts remain unchanged. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 39 references and research-positioning passages are retained, including the distinctions from logit-based unlearning and Shifting Attention to Relevance.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 20 October 2025, to v3, dated 17 April 2026. Prose, terminology and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, formatting and placement are identical. The mathematical argument reversal in Equation (5) does not change the document's layout.

improvement.justification: The only substantive revision reverses the retention KL in Equation (5), but v3 supplies no explanation or validation establishing that this corrects the intended objective. Results and appendices are unchanged, and Appendix A analyzes only suppression gradients. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether the revision improves mathematical fidelity or leaves a different objective unsupported by the reported experiments.
